name: City Council Regular Meeting of February 26, 2025
minutes_text:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF FEBRUARY 26, 2025

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:01 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Marisol Cortez, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Sheila Crippen-Thomas, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Cindy Galvan, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Martin Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Viviana Longoria, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Julia Ruedas, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Councilmember Dr. Ruedas
  s) Councilmember Herrera  7-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete
  all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council
  completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short
  recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event
  the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by
  7:00 p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the
  meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the
  public wish to address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City
  Council shall allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to
  going into Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner
  prescribed on page 1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed
  session; and (ii) be subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous
  minutes total per speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items
  of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 and 4.2. Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed
  Session at approximately 6:02 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened
  from Closed Session at approximately 7:12 p.m.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  City Council received a report from legal counsel, feedback was provided,
  but no final action taken.

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 26, 2025

  Officers Association; and El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma Martinez, City Manager; and Rigoberto
  Gutierrez, Human Resources/Risk Management Director.

  City Council received a report from legal counsel, feedback was provided,
  but no final action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain. Present

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  Joseph Ramirez, 3rd Grade Student from Payne Elementary
  School. Present

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Presentation by the City Council to Joseph Ramirez from Payne Elementary
  School for Leading the Pledge of Allegiance. Present

  7.2  Presentation by the City Council to Custody Officer Bob Elkin from the El Monte
  Police Department for his Outstanding Efforts and Life-Saving Actions. Present

  7.3  Presentation by the City Council to the Los Angeles County Fire Station in the City
  of El Monte, Station No. 166, 167, 168, and 169 for their Outstanding Service
  During the Easton and Palisades Fire. Present

  7.4  Presentation by the City Council to Our Gremlin Cheer Team from the El
  Monte/South El Monte Jets for their Incredible Milestone, Taking 1st Place at the
  Jamz Cheer Competition and Earning the Title of National Champions on February
  1, 2025. Present

  7.5  Presentation by the City Council to Arnold Barboza Jr. WBO Interim Title
  Champion. Present

Break at 7:52 pm
Return at 8:03 pm

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 26, 2025

  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.
  Am Bowes – Provided updates for the library.

  Charles Hoffman – Spoke about the Historical Museum Open House on March 1, 2025
  from 1:00 pm to 3:00 pm.

  Cosme Jimenez – Spoke about Item 14.1.

  Transgender Queen – Spoke about various items.

  Armando Herman – Spoke about various items.
  Tony Garcia – Requested an extension to his current contract for the Goody’s property.

9.  CITY TREASURER’S REPORT:

  9.1  Transmittal of the Treasurer’s Cash and Investment Report for the Quarter Ended
  December 31, 2024.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Receive and file the Treasurer’s Cash and Investment Report for the quarter
  ended December 31, 2024.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No:  N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Receive and file the report.

10.  DEMAND RESOLUTION NO. D-725

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA,
  ALLOWING CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT
  OF WHICH THE SAME ARE TO BE PAID.

  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF EL MONTE, CALIFORNIA, DOES RESOLVE AS
  FOLLOWS: SECTION 1. That the attached list of claims and demands totaling
  $4,653,260.35 have been examined by the City Treasurer and that warrant numbers
  1128559 through 1129050, and the payroll period January 16, 2025 through January 31,
  2025 inclusive are hereby allowed in the amounts and ordered paid out of the respective
  funds as set forth.

  m) Councilmember Crippen-Thomas
  s) Councilmember Galvan  7-0

11.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES: None

12.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda. One
  or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be discussed,
  considered, and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded motion of any
  member of the Council with the approval of a majority of the Council quorum.

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 26, 2025

12.1  Waiver of Full Reading of Ordinance(s).

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Approval to waive full reading (except title) of all ordinances appearing on the
  City Council agenda as authorized under Government Code Section 36934,
  unless otherwise directed by the City Council.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No:  N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Crippen-Thomas  7-0

12.2  Consideration and Approval of the Incorporation of New Policies Into the City of El
  Monte’s Administrative Policies and Procedures Manual.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BU SINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Consider and approve the incorporation of the following new policies into the
  City of El Monte Administrative Policies and Procedures Manual:
  . City-Wide Budget Policy;
  a. Reserve Policy;
  b. Travel Expense Policy; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee, to immediately implement and
  administer said policies.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No:  N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  m) Councilmember Galvan
  s) Councilmember Longoria  7-0

12.3  Consideration to Accept the Zone 3 Street Improvement Project, CIP 053, as
  Complete and File the Notice of Completion with the Los Angeles County
  Recorder’s Office.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BU SINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Consider and accept the Zone 3 Street Improvement Project, CIP 053 as
  complete and authorize staff to file the Notice of Completion with the Los
  Angeles County Recorder’s Office; and
  2. Authorize staff to release the retention 35 days after the acceptance by the City
  Council.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No:  N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Crippen-Thomas  7-0

12.4  Consideration and Approval to Authorize the Execution of the Memorandum of
  Agreement Between the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments and the City
  of El Monte Documenting Details of the Transaction for Corazon Del Valle Event.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BU SINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 26, 2025

  1. Consider, approve, and authorize the City Manager, or her designee, to
  execute the Memorandum of Agreement between the San Gabriel Valley
  Council of Governments and the Cities of El Monte and South El Monte for
  planning and hosting the Active Streets: Corazón del Valle 2025 Event; and
  2. Authorize the use of TDA funds for in-kind services for an amount not-to-
  exceed $25,000 for the Open Streets Event.

  Total Cost: $25,000  Account No:  Various
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? Yes

  m) Councilmember Dr. Ruedas
  s) Councilmember Crippen-Thomas  7-0

  12.5  Consideration and Approval of a Purchase Order with TrueLine Construction &
  Surfacing for the Resurfacing and Refitting of the Basketball and Pickleball Courts
  at Mountain View Park for a Not-to-Exceed Amount of $55,000.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BU SINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Consider and approve a purchase order with TrueLine Construction &
  Surfacing for the resurfacing and refitting of the basketball and pickleball courts
  at Mountain View Park for a not-to-exceed amount of $55,000.

  Total Cost: $55,000  Account No:  286-56-531-8121
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? Yes

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Crippen-Thomas  7-0

  12.6  Consideration and Approval of a Purchase Order with AME Builders, Inc. for the
  Removal and Replacement of the Mountain View Park Picnic Shelter Roof for a
  Not-to-Exceed Amount of $60,000.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BU SINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Consider and approve a purchase order with AME Builders, Inc. for the removal
  and replacement of the Mountain View Park Picnic Shelter Roof for a not-to-
  exceed amount of $60,000.

  Total Cost: $60,000  Account No:  286-56-531-8121
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? Yes

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Crippen-Thomas  7-0

13.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  Members of the public wishing to address the Council on any item of business agendized
  under this Public Hearing portion of the agenda are asked to submit a speaker card for
  each Public Hearing item of business they wish to address the Council on. Each speaker
  will be allotted three (3) continuous minutes per Public Hearing item. Members of the
  public are asked to submit speaker cards to the City Clerk or the Sergeant-of-Arms before
  the Council’s approval of the agenda, if possible. The Council is under no obligation to
  recognize a speaker who submits a speaker card for a particular Public Hearing item of
  business after the public comment portion of the public hearing for that item has closed.

  13.1  A Public Hearing to Consider and Approve an Ordinance Amending Certain
  Provisions of Chapter 10.08 (Speed Limits) of Title 10 (Vehicles and Traffic) of the
  El Monte Municipal Code Relating to Speed Limits on City Streets.
  RECOMMENDATION OF BU SINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 26, 2025

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Open the public hearing;

  2. Receive a brief presentation from City staff and pose questions to City staff;
  3. Receive public comment, if any;
  4. Close the public hearing;
  5. Adopt the attached Ordinance approving the amendments to the El Monte
  Municipal Code relating to speed limits on City streets; and
  6. Approve the update to the 2023 City of El Monte Engineering and Traffic
  Survey.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No:  N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A
  Ordinance No. 3046

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Galvan  7-0

  13.2  A Public Hearing Regarding Proposed Zoning Amendments and Related
  Environmental Review Approvals Affecting Properties Along the Garvey Avenue
  Corridor and 5-Points Area Comprised of an Approximately 2.2 Mile Segment of
  Garvey Avenue, Approximately 50 Feet East of Potrero Avenue to a Location
  Approximately 430 Feet West of the Intersection of Garvey Avenue, Valley
  Boulevard, Mountain View Road and Cosgwell Road.

  IMPORTANT UPDATE: This previously noticed action item has been continued
  indefinitely so that the City may first conduct a separate community meeting to
  better explain the proposed amendments and to receive public input. The
  community meeting will be held on a date, time and location to be determined.

14.  REGULAR AGENDA:

  14.1  Consideration and Approval to Amend the Fire Protection and Emergency Medical
  Services Agreement with the Los Angeles County Fire to Reflect Increases in the
  Annual Fee Limitation, Cola Assumption, Employee Benefits, And Department
  Overhead For Fiscal Year 2025-26 Through 2028-29

  RECOMMENDATION OF BU SINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Amendment to the Fire Protection and Emergency Medical
  Services Agreement with the Los Angeles County Fire District to reflect
  increases in the Annual Fee Limitation, COLA Assumption, Employee Benefits,

  6
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 26, 2025

  and department overhead for Fiscal Year 2025-26 through 2028-29. The
  amount for each fiscal year will be included in the budget for each fiscal year;
  and
  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Amendment to the Fire Protection
  and Emergency Medical Services Agreement with Los Angeles County Fire
  and all other corresponding documents.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No:  N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Dr. Ruedas  7-0

15.  CITY ATTORNEY’S AGENDA: None

16.  CITY MANAGER’S AGENDA:

  Welcomed the new Public Works Director Jerry Moreno.

  16.1  Update Regarding the City’s Credit Rating.

  Reported that the City’s SMP just affirmed the City’s A+ rating for the pension
  obligation bonds which were issued five (5) years ago.

  Mayor Ancona requested a copy of the report.

17.  WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS: None

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18A.1 Request for Standing Meetings with the City Manager on the Second and
  Fourth Monday of each Month at 8:00 A.M. at City Hall to Review the
  Agenda.

  18A.2 Discussion and Request for Economic Development Ad Hoc Meetings to
  Address Development Concerns.

  Received scheduled meetings from staff. Council is excited to have
  these meetings. Request to have all of the meetings on the Council’s
  meetings.

  18A.3 Discussion and Follow Up on Previous Discussion with the City Manager
  for a Victory Celebration Honoring Arnold Barboza Jr. the WBO Interim Title
  Champion.

  Is not available to have a celebration any time soon because he is
  getting ready for his fight.

  Last week had the opportunity to join Congressman Gil Cisneros
  Round Table for Mayors and City Managers. Spoke about the needs
  and concerns for the region and for the City including the $10M for
  Pioneer Park.

  Another item discussed was the waste removal from the Eaton Fire.
  There is a location in El Monte that was flagged for the Phase 2.

  7
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 26, 2025

18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Cortez

  Was able to chair last Wednesday’s Coordinating Council meeting. There
  were about 20 attendees.

  Spoke about celebrations, recognitions, and promotions of businesses.

18C.  Councilwoman Crippen-Thomas

  Reminded everyone of the first community event for District 1 at Cherrylee.

  Great grand opening today at US Bank, they are excited to be here, staff did
  a great job.

18D.  Councilwoman Galvan

18E.  Councilman Herrera

  Thanked colleagues for attending the Coordinating Council meeting.

  Congratulated Mr. Jerry Moreno. Congratulated the Executive Team on the
  A+ Rating.

  Had the opportunity to attend the presentation given by the School Resource
  Officers regarding drug awareness.

18F.  Councilwoman Longoria

18G.  Councilwoman Dr. Ruedas

  Thanked staff for the scheduling of the ad hoc meetings and for sharing the
  information.

  Requested update on the Arden Drive complete streets project from Valley
  Boulevard to Lower Azusa Road.

  Congratulated and thanked the businesses in the City. Recognized Good
  Donut for their 14 year anniversary.

  Mayor Ancona – El Monte Phillies this Saturday starting at 9:00 am. Also this
  weekend is garage sale weekend.

  Mayor Pro Tem Cortez – Community outreach meeting at 11:00 am at
  Mountain View Park

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of February 26, 2025

19.  ADJOURNMENT:

  At 9:44 p.m.
  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Galvan
  Adjourn the meeting

  The next Regular Meeting of the City Council will be held on March 12, 2025 at 6:00 p.m.
  This Agenda will be posted on the City’s website, www.ci.el-monte.ca.us, and physically
  posted no less than 72 hours prior to the start of the subject regular meeting. Although it
  is the City’s practice and desire to electronically post a copy of this Agenda along with
  supporting material as part of its website posting, the size or formatting of certain
  supporting materials may render their website posting infeasible. Nevertheless, all
  supporting materials related to any item on this Agenda, that is made available to the
  members of the council may be inspected by members of the public at the City Clerk’s
  Office located at 11333 Valley Boulevard, El Monte, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am
  – 5:30 pm. For more information, please call the City Clerk’s Office at 626-580-2016.

  All public meetings and events sponsored or conducted by the City of El Monte are held
  in sites accessible to persons with disabilities. Requests for accommodations may be
  made by calling the office of the City Clerk at (626) 580-2016 at least three (3) working
  days prior to the event, if possible. This Agenda and copies of documents distributed at
  the meeting are available in alternative formats upon request.
